config.description: Columnar chart for 735 ÷ 35 (main 3, flag 5): 7÷3 writes 2 remainder 1; the bring-down forms 13; the flag product 2×5=10 is subtracted in the tens column to leave 3; quotient 21 assembled by place.
config.textual_equivalent: 735 ÷ 35 with main 3 and flag 5: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1; bring down 3 to form 13; subtract flag product 10 to leave 3; continue to quotient 21.

examples.problem_statement: Divide 735 by 35 using the Dhvajanka Sutra (Flag Division method).

solution.description: Rewrite the divisor 35 as the main digit 3 with the 5 raised as a flag, so the actual dividing is done by 3 alone and the flag digit is paid back later as an adjustment.
Divide the leading digit 7 of the dividend by the main divisor 3. This gives the first quotient digit 2 and leaves a remainder of 1.
Because the flag digit 5 was set aside in step 1, multiply the quotient digit 2 just found by that flag to get the adjustment 10, which is what the flag still owes.

Place the remainder 1 in front of the next dividend digit 3 to form the gross dividend 13, then subtract the flag adjustment 10 from it. The corrected working value is 3, which carries into the units column.
Read the quotient digits off in the order they were produced to get 21, and note that nothing is left over, so 735 divided by 35 is exactly 21.

common_mistakes: Dividing 7 by the whole divisor 35 instead of by the main digit 3, which stalls the method before it starts.
Forgetting to subtract the flag product 10 from the gross dividend 13 and carrying 13 forward, which inflates the next quotient digit.
repair_note: Rewrote all five descriptions so each narrates its own operation and result in the context of 735 divided by 35 (flag split, first quotient digit, flag product 10, gross dividend 13 corrected to 3, final quotient 21). technique_name 'division' and scaffold place_value_chart already match the columnar work and were left alone. Added two hazards specific to these numbers; no common_mistakes filler was present.

config.description: Columnar chart for 960 ÷ 32 (main 3, flag 2): quotient digit 3 from the hundreds column, flag product 3×2=6 subtracted to leave working dividend 90 flowing into the next column, building quotient 30.
config.textual_equivalent: 960 ÷ 32 with main 3 and flag 2: 9 ÷ 3 = 3; flag product 3×2 = 6; 96 − 6 = 90 carried into the next column; continue to quotient 30.

examples.problem_statement: Divide 960 by 32 using the Dhvajanka Sutra (Flag Division method).

solution.description: Rewrite the divisor 32 as the main digit 3 with the 2 raised as a flag, so the dividing is carried out by 3 and the flag digit 2 is compensated for by a later adjustment.
Divide the leading digit 9 by the main divisor 3, which gives 3 as the tentative first quotient digit. It is tentative because the flag has not yet been accounted for.
Multiply the tentative quotient digit 3 by the flag digit 2 to get 6, the correction the flag demands before the next digit can be found.
Subtract that adjustment of 6 from the first two digits of the dividend, 96, leaving the working value 90 to continue the division with.

Compare the working value 90 with the divisor 32: the estimate is about 2.8, which rounds to the leading digit 3 already found, so the trial quotient is 30. Checking against the original dividend confirms 960 divided by 32 is exactly 30.

common_mistakes: Stopping at the tentative digit 3 and reporting the quotient as 3 instead of carrying it into the tens place to get 30.
Adding the flag product 6 to 96 instead of subtracting it, which sends the working value the wrong way.
repair_note: Rewrote all five descriptions against their own operations for 960 divided by 32, including step 5, whose result estimates 90 divided by 32 as about 2.8, rounds to the leading digit 3 already found and confirms the quotient 30. Scaffold place_value_chart and technique_name 'division' match the work. Added two example-specific mistakes.

config.description: Straight-division chart for 1848 ÷ 168 (main 16, flag 8): the dividend spans four place columns with the leading digits grouped for the two-digit main; 184÷16 writes 11 remainder 8; the remainder prefixes the brought-down 8 to make 88; the flag product 88 is subtracted in the units column to leave 0.
config.textual_equivalent: 1848 ÷ 168 with main 16 and flag 8: 184 ÷ 16 = 11 remainder 8; bring down 8 to form 88; subtract flag product 11×8 = 88 to leave 0; quotient 11.

examples.problem_statement: Divide 1848 by 168 using the Dhvajanka Sutra (Flag Division method).

solution.description: Split divisor into main part (16) and flag digit (8). For 3-digit divisors, use first two digits as main.

solution.operation: Divide first digits by main divisor
solution.description: Divide first three digits (184) by main part (16). Quotient is 11, remainder is 8.
Multiply tentative quotient (11) by flag digit (8).
Bring down next digit (8) to remainder (8) giving 88. Subtract flag adjustment (88) to get 0.
Verify: 11 × 168 = 1848, confirming the quotient is correct.

repair_note: Every description already narrates its own operation and result for 1848 divided by 168 (main 16, flag 8; 184 divided by 16 is 11 remainder 8; gross 88 minus flag product 88 is 0; verification 11 times 168). technique_name and place_value_chart scaffold match the steps, and no common_mistakes filler was present, so nothing was altered.

config.description: Straight-division chart for 2946 ÷ 231 (main 23, flag 1): the dividend spans four place columns with the leading digits grouped for the two-digit main; 294÷23 writes 12 remainder 18; the remainder prefixes the brought-down 6 to make 186; the flag product 12 is subtracted, leaving final remainder 174.
config.textual_equivalent: 2946 ÷ 231 with main 23 and flag 1: 294 ÷ 23 = 12 remainder 18; bring down 6 to form 186; subtract flag product 12 to leave 174; quotient 12 remainder 174.

examples.problem_statement: Divide 2946 by 231 using the Dhvajanka Sutra (Flag Division method).

solution.description: Rewrite the divisor 231 as the two-digit main part 23 with the final digit 1 raised as a flag, since a three-digit divisor keeps its first two digits as the working divisor.
Divide the first three digits of the dividend, 294, by the main part 23. This gives the quotient 12 and leaves a remainder of 18.
Multiply the quotient 12 just found by the flag digit 1 to get the adjustment 12, the amount the flag digit contributes to the next column.
Put the remainder 18 in front of the last dividend digit 6 to form the gross value 186, then subtract the flag adjustment 12, leaving 174.

Test whether the division can continue: 174 is smaller than the divisor 231, so no further quotient digit can be formed. That fixes the quotient at 12 with 174 left over, and 231 times 12 is 2772, which is 174 short of 2946.
State the result in division form: 2946 equals 231 times 12 plus 174, so the quotient is 12 and the remainder is 174.

common_mistakes: Reporting 186 as the remainder without first subtracting the flag adjustment 12.
Forcing the division to come out even and pushing the quotient to 13, even though 231 times 13 is 3003, which overshoots 2946.
repair_note: Rewrote the six descriptions to name the actual quantities of 2946 divided by 231 (main 23, flag 1; 294 divided by 23 is 12 remainder 18; gross 186 minus flag product 12 is 174) and to explain why step 5 stops the division. Scaffold and technique_name already matched. Added two mistakes tied to the non-zero remainder.

config.description: Divisor x+3 split into main x | flag 3 lanes over the coefficient row 1|2|−5|−6; each quotient term sends a diagonal crosswise product (3x², −3x, −6) into the next coefficient's adjustment lane, building x² − x − 2 with remainder 0.
config.textual_equivalent: (x³ + 2x² − 5x − 6) ÷ (x + 3), main x flag 3: x³ ÷ x = x², crosswise 3x² adjusts 2x² to −x²; −x² ÷ x = −x, crosswise −3x adjusts −5x to −2x; −2x ÷ x = −2, crosswise −6 leaves remainder 0; quotient x² − x − 2.

examples.problem_statement: Divide (x³ + 2x² - 5x - 6) by (x + 3) using the Dhvajanka Sutra (Flag Division method for polynomials).

solution.description: Split the divisor x + 3 the same way a numeric divisor is split: the leading term x becomes the main part and the constant 3 is raised as the flag.
Lay out the work with the dividend x cubed plus 2x squared minus 5x minus 6 above the split divisor, so each quotient term can be found from the main part and corrected by the flag.

solution.result: x^{3} ÷ x = x^{2} (first term of quotient)
solution.description: Divide the leading term of the dividend by the main part: x cubed divided by x gives x squared, the first term of the quotient.
Multiply that quotient term x squared by the flag 3, giving the crosswise product 3x squared that must be paid back in the next column.
Subtract the crosswise product from the x squared coefficient of the dividend: 2x squared minus 3x squared leaves negative x squared as the new leading term.
Divide the new leading term by the main part: negative x squared divided by x gives negative x, the second term of the quotient, and the working dividend is now negative x squared minus 5x minus 6.
Multiply the new quotient term negative x by the flag 3 to get negative 3x, then subtract it from the x coefficient: minus 5x minus minus 3x leaves minus 2x.
Divide the leading term of the reduced dividend by the main part once more: negative 2x divided by x gives negative 2, the third and last term of the quotient.

Multiply the final quotient term negative 2 by the flag 3 to get negative 6, and subtract it from the constant minus 6. Nothing is left, so the remainder is zero and x + 3 divides the dividend exactly.

common_mistakes: Adding the crosswise product instead of subtracting it, so the x squared coefficient becomes 5x squared rather than negative x squared.
Dropping the sign of a quotient term and using x instead of negative x for the crosswise product in the next column.
repair_note: Rewrote the nine descriptions so each states the term being divided, the crosswise flag product and the coefficient it corrects, replacing generic 'continue the division' prose. LaTeX-style fragments were kept out of the prose. technique_name 'polynomial division' and the arrow_matrix scaffold match the crosswise coefficient work. Added two sign-related mistakes.

solution.description: Choose 10 as the base, since 8 lies close to it and 10 is the nearest power of ten. Every later step measures 8 against this base.

solution.operation: Find the deficiency from the base
solution.description: Measure 8 against the base: it sits 2 below 10, so the deviation is recorded as -2. The sign is what tells the later steps whether to add or take away.

The Yavadunam Sutra states: 'Whatever the deficiency, lessen by that amount and set up the square of the deficiency.' For squaring, the left part is (base + 2×deviation) and the right part is (deviation)².
Add twice the deficiency to the base: 2 times -2 is -4, and 10 minus 4 gives the left part 6.
Square the deviation to get the right part: -2 times -2 is 4. Two like signs multiply to a positive, so the right part is positive whichever side of the base the number falls on.

solution.operation: Pad the right part to 1 digit(s)
solution.description: The base 10 has one zero, so the right part is allowed exactly one digit. Here 4 is already a single digit, so no leading zero has to be added.
Write the left part 6 immediately followed by the one-digit right part 4 to read off the square of 8, which is 64.
Check the answer by an independent route, expanding (10 minus 2) squared with the binomial identity for (a plus or minus b) squared. It returns 64, confirming the sutra's result.

common_mistakes: Writing the deficiency itself, 2, in the right part instead of its square, giving 62 rather than 64.
Subtracting the deficiency only once from the base, so the left part comes out as 8 instead of 10 plus 2 times minus 2, which is 6.
repair_note: Rewrote seven of the eight descriptions so each names the deviation, left part, right part and answer for the square of 8 instead of reciting generic template prose; the step 3 description already states the sutra it sits on and was kept. Scaffold textual_scaffold is correct because the method manipulates no visual structure, and technique_name 'yavadunam' matches the steps. Replaced the four boilerplate common_mistakes, which were identical across every template in this family and described padding and carry hazards that do not arise with a one-digit right part, with two mistakes a learner would actually make with these numbers.
